name: The Historic Town and Archaeological Site of Gedi
description: Hidden in the Arabuko-Sokoke forest near Kenya's Indian Ocean coast, Gedi is an abandoned Swahili town that flourished between the 10th and 17th centuries. Walking its walled grounds, you pass roofless mosques, a palace, stone houses and distinctive pillar tombs, all built from coral rag. Imported beads, pottery and coins found here show how far its trade reached across the ocean.
